in_latin.name: Alyssa
in_latin.long_meaning: Alyssa est nomen femininum, quod significat libertatem animi et voluntatem. Ex Hebraeis radicibus בטוור et שס ב אול, nomen Alyssa significat animam libera et autonoma. In ecclesiis Christianis, nomen Alyssa est utilis ad designare personas liberales et voluntarias.

historical_references.reference: Alyssa, the heroine of the ancient Greek legend, was said to be a beautiful nymph who fell in love with Leucippus, a mortal shepherd. When Leucippus was called away to war, Alyssa pledged her love and vowed to wait for him. However, believing him to be dead, she eventually married another man. When Leucippus returned, he was filled with rage and killed Alyssa's new husband, then took his own life in sorrow. Alyssa's name was later adopted by early Christians as a symbol of faithfulness and devotion.

The name was also used in various religious texts and artworks, symbolizing faith and devotion.
